explain.say: That was fine when travel was slow, but then came trains. See the train at 1840? Timetables with many local times were confusing, so the Great Western Railway ran all its trains on London time. People called it railway time. Can you see why trains needed one time?

faq.a: Before railways, each town set its clocks by the Sun, with 12 noon when the Sun was highest. Towns further west were a few minutes behind towns further east.
asks: Why did towns have different times?

faq.a: One time used by a railway for all its stations and timetables. In Britain it was London time, first used across the Great Western Railway in 1840.
asks: Why did trains need the same time?

faq.q: Why is Greenwich at zero longitude?
faq.a: In 1884, the International Meridian Conference in Washington chose the line through the Royal Observatory at Greenwich. Most of the world's ships already used Greenwich charts.

faq.q: When did America get time zones?
faq.a: On 18 November 1883, the US and Canadian railways began using four standard time zones. The US made them law in 1918.
asks: Who made time zones in America?

faq.q: Does every country use whole-hour time zones?
faq.a: Most use whole hours from Greenwich, but some use half or quarter hours. India is 5 and a half hours ahead, and Nepal is 5 hours 45 minutes ahead.
asks: Why is India's time zone half an hour?

facts: The Great Western Railway adopted London time across its network in November 1840.
The International Meridian Conference of 1884 chose Greenwich as the Prime Meridian, zero degrees longitude.
